info.title: Mesub API
info.description: Recurring payments on Solana. Every route takes the project's API key as a bearer token. Fields are in snake case, dates are ISO 8601 strings in UTC, and token amounts are strings in the token's smallest unit.

get.description:
Whether a customer may use a plan, and what explains the answer. Always 200 for a customer, subscribed or not: a customer who never subscribed answers `access: false` with `status: "none"`. The 404 is about the slug, never about them.

Leave `plan` out to get every plan of the project the customer has anything on.

On a plan with an end date, nobody has access past that date: `access` is false from the plan's end on and `access_until` is never later, whatever period was paid for. The subscription turns `ended` within minutes of it, so `status` can still read `active` or `unpaid` for that long with `access` false. Gate on `access`.

One plan: its name, its price in the smallest unit and as a person counts it, its period, its token, its status, its end date, and whether it takes new subscribers now.

post.description:
Reserves a subscription to one of your plans for the wallet named, and builds what that wallet signs: the terms, as a message, then the transaction, without sending it. Hand both to [Submit](/reference/subscriptions/submit).

Called again for the same plan, wallet and customer while nothing has landed, it answers the same subscription with a fresh transaction. The customer is the `external_id`, else the `email`, else nobody. Another customer naming the same wallet gets a subscription of its own: only the one the wallet signs for lands.

A wallet whose subscription to this plan stopped comes back over its existing authorisation: a new subscription, with `costs.rent` at zero.

On a plan with an end date, `terms.message` says that the last charge is in full and that access stops when the plan ends. When the plan ends before a second charge can be made, it says the charge is a single one.

x-mesub.limit: 60 calls a minute per API key
x-mesub.confirm: This reserves a real subscription in the project the key belongs to. It charges nothing until a wallet signs and you submit.

get.description:
A customer's subscriptions to your project's plans, newest first: what a "my subscriptions" page needs. A customer with nothing is not an error: `data` is empty.

Expired checkouts are listed too, and `access` says they grant nothing. A subscription replaced by a newer one of the same wallet (`superseded`) is left out, though its id still answers on [Retrieve](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve).

post.description:
Relays what the wallet signed: the transaction and the terms. Mesub checks both signatures, co-signs, sends the transaction and waits for the chain, so this call is slow by design: up to 90 seconds.

Safe to send again unchanged. Mesub recognises what it already co-signed and answers from the chain, so a customer is never charged twice.

get.description:
One subscription: its status, whether it grants access and until when, its wallet, email and `external_id`, the period it last paid for, and what comes next. `access`, `payment_status` and `access_until` are what [Check access](/reference/access/check) answers for it.

A `superseded` id, left out of the list, still answers here, so an id you stored keeps working.

On a plan with an end date, `access` is false from that date on and `access_until` is never later than it, whatever period was paid for. `next_charge_at` and `next_retry_at` are null once the plan ends before the charge or the retry.

The charges of one subscription, newest first, and what it paid since it began: what a screen showing a customer one subscription with its payments needs.

post.description:
Builds the transaction that cancels an `active`, `unpaid` or `stopped` subscription. The subscription's own wallet signs and sends it, then you [confirm](/reference/manage/confirm-cancel). Nothing changes until the confirmation.

A subscription that is paid up keeps its access until the end of the period. A late or stopped one has none, and its missed period is never collected.

post.description:
The first payment landed.

Mesub posts this to every endpoint of the project subscribed to it. Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds.

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: The event's id, the same on every retry. Deduplicate on it.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: When this attempt was sent, in Unix seconds.

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description: `v1,` then the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body`, keyed with the endpoint's signing secret, the Standard Webhooks way.

data.description: The subscription, as [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) answers it when the delivery is first attempted, plus `detail`, which is the event's own.

test.description: True on a test delivery of this event, sent by hand from the dashboard. Absent otherwise.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else, a redirect included, counts as a failure and is retried.

post.description:
A renewal is near, and whether it can pay.

Sent once per period, when the subscription enters the last quarter of it and three days before the charge at most, whether the charge can pay or not. Mesub reads the customer's wallet at that moment: `detail` is that reading, not a promise, and the charge itself answers with `subscription.renewed` or `subscription.payment_failed`. An endpoint receives it only if this event is selected for it.

Not sent for a charge that cannot happen: on a plan with an end date, a subscription in its last period has no renewal, and gets no event.

Mesub posts this to every endpoint of the project subscribed to it. Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description:
A charge missed.

`detail` says what comes next. On a plan with an end date, the plan can end before the next retry: `detail.next_retry_at` is then null and `detail.retries_left` is 0, and the subscription ends at the plan's end with `subscription.ended`.

Mesub posts this to every endpoint of the project subscribed to it. Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds.

apiKey.description: The project's API key, which starts with `SUB_`. Keep it on your server.

message.description: A sentence for a person. It may be reworded any day: do not branch on it. A validation error answers a list of reasons.

code.description: What a program reads. A code is never renamed or reused, but new ones are added: keep a default branch.

retryable.description: Whether the same request, sent again unchanged, may succeed later.

id.description: The id of the project the API key belongs to.

AccessAttempt.description: One charge, as you may show it to the customer it concerns.

outcome.description: `skipped`: nothing was sent because the chain said it could not work. `rejected`: sent and refused. `blocked`: not tried, and never the customer's doing.

reason.description: Why it did not pay. Null on a paid one.

amount.description: In the token's smallest unit, as a string.

signature.description: The transaction. Null when nothing was sent.

AccessAnswer.title: With a plan
AccessAnswer.description: Whether the customer has access to the plan, and what explains the answer.

wallet.description: The wallet the answer is about. Asked by `wallet`, that wallet. Asked by `external_id` or `email`, the one that pays, or null when the customer has nothing on this plan.

access.description: The only field a guard needs. False from the plan's end date on, whatever period was paid for.

status.description: Where the subscription stands. `none` for a customer who never subscribed to this plan. Mesub may add a status later: keep a default branch. For a few minutes after a plan's end date it can still read `active` or `unpaid` with `access` false, never `ended` with `access` true: gate on `access`.

paused.description: True on a seat parked over the project's subscriber limit: the status stays as it was, nothing is charged, and access runs to the end of the period already paid.

end_reason.description: Why it ended. Set only when `status` is `ended`. Null on every other status, and on an old subscription that ended with no reason recorded.

late_reason.description: Why a payment is late, as the last failed charge found it. Set only when `status` is `unpaid`. Null on every other status, and when Mesub cannot name the cause.

payment_status.description: `late` while a charge missed and a retry is pending. `none` where nothing is being billed.

subscribed_since.description: The start of the current subscription.

first_subscribed_at.description: The start of the very first one. Differs for a customer who left and came back.

current_period_end.description: The end of the period last paid for.

cancelled_at.description: When they asked to stop, not when access ends.

access_until.description: When access ends unless a charge renews it. Never later than the plan's end date, where access stops for everybody. Null while `access` is false.

next_charge_at.description: The next charge. Null when a retry is pending instead, and when the plan's end date leaves no charge to make: a subscription in its last period has none.

next_retry_at.description: The next retry of a missed charge. Null when the plan ends before it.

retry_deadline.description: On Free only: when retries by hand close for the missed period, or the plan's end date when that comes first.

attempts.description: The last charges, newest first, five at most. Present only when asked with `attempts=true`.

revalidate_after.description: Seconds this answer stays true. The SDK caches it for that long.

AccessList.title: Without a plan
AccessList.description: Every plan of the project the customer has anything on, sorted by slug. Maybe none.

plans.description: One answer per plan, as with `plan`.

revalidate_after.description: Seconds this list stays true: the soonest of its plans'.

Plan.description: A plan as your server reads it, to build a pricing page of your own.

slug.description: How your code names the plan.

name.description: The plan's name as you filled it, or its slug when you filled none.

amount.description: The price per period, in the token's smallest unit, as a string.

amount_display.description: The price as a person counts it: `9.99`.

symbol.description: The token's symbol. Null for a token Mesub cannot vouch for.

period_hours.description: The length of a period, in hours. 720 is thirty days.

network.description: The Solana cluster the plan is on.

status.description: `sunset`: closed to new subscribers, its subscribers still paying until `ends_at`.

available.description: Whether it takes new subscribers now: active, before its end date, and the project not full.

ends_at.description: The plan's end date: when it stops charging, and when access stops for every subscriber, whatever period they paid for. Set on every sunset plan. Null when it has no end.

Subscription.description: One subscription to one of your project's plans.

status.description: Where it stands. Unlike `GET /v1/access`, may be `expired`: a checkout nobody signed. `cancelled` while the cancellation runs, `ended` once its end passed. For a few minutes after a plan's end date it can still read `active` or `unpaid` with `access` false, never `ended` with `access` true.

paused.description: True on a seat parked over the project's subscriber limit, its status unchanged.

end_reason.description: Why it ended. Set only when `status` is `ended`. Null on every other status, and on an old subscription that ended with no reason recorded.

late_reason.description: Why a payment is late, as the last failed charge found it. Set only when `status` is `unpaid`. Null on every other status, and when Mesub cannot name the cause.

access.description: Whether this subscription grants access now, as `GET /v1/access` answers it. False from the plan's end date on, whatever period was paid for.

payment_status.description: `late` while a charge missed and a retry is pending. `none` where nothing is being billed.

email.description: Where the customer's notices go, as given at creation.

external_id.description: Your own id for the customer, as given at creation.

current_period_start.description: The start of the period last paid for. Null before the first.

next_charge_at.description: The next charge on a running subscription. Null when a retry is pending instead, and when the plan's end date leaves no charge to make: a subscription in its last period has none.

next_retry_at.description: The next retry on a late one. Null when the plan ends before it.

retry_deadline.description: On Free only: when retries by hand close for the missed period, or the plan's end date when that comes first.

next_retry_number.description: Which retry comes at `next_retry_at`: 1 is the first after the missed charge. Null unless Mesub retries on its own, and when `next_retry_at` is null.

retries_allowed.description: How many retries the missed period gets. Null unless Mesub retries on its own.

access_until.description: When access ends unless a charge renews it. Never later than the plan's end date, where access stops for everybody. Null while `access` is false.

outcome.description: `skipped`: nothing was sent because the chain said it could not work. `rejected`: sent and refused. `blocked`: not tried, and never the customer's doing.

reason.description: Why it did not pay, short and stable. Null on a paid one.

amount.description: In the token's smallest unit, as a string. What a paid one moved, what any other asked for.

signature.description: The transaction. Null when nothing was sent.

retry.description: Whether the subscription had already failed on this period.

retry_number.description: Which retry of the plan's it was: 1 is the first after the missed charge. Null on a first try.

retries_allowed.description: Out of how many, as recorded when it ran.

period_start.description: The start of the period it was for.

paid.description: Counted over every paid charge since the subscription began, not over the page.

amount.description: The sum, in the token's smallest unit, as a string.

Costs.description: What subscribing costs the wallet in SOL, in lamports, as strings.

rent.description: A deposit the customer gets back when the subscription is closed.

authority.description: Null when the customer already has an authority for that token.

id.description: Keep it: every later call names it.

transaction.description: Base64, signed by nobody. The wallet signs it without sending it.

last_valid_block_height.description: The block height after which the transaction can no longer land.

message.description: Plain text, one fact per line. The wallet signs it as is, before the transaction.

expires_at.description: Five minutes after the call. Both signatures must come back before it.

reason.description: Present only when nothing was settled, or when what landed is not what Mesub built. It says why.

transaction.description: Base64, signed by nobody. The subscription's own wallet signs and sends it.

last_valid_block_height.description: The block height after which the transaction can no longer land.
